about: What the smallest terminal application with its agent endpoint loads (CF1's F4; terminal design §5, the second tier): omui.size.terminal-agent built as dist builds it (-O3, NDEBUG) with its symbol table kept, the allocated sections of its program counted (.bss and the symbols left out). Bytes.

budgets.why: The terminal design's second tier (§5, D-219): 2 MB — the first tier's 1 MB and about 1 MB for the endpoint (the bus, JSON, the spec's types). Measured 5,183,427 B (2026-11-26, GCC 16 on Linux x64, the system's C++ runtime; 5,190,968 B stripped): over it, a red with the first tier's. Over terminal's 3,382,445 B the endpoint costs 1,800,982 B: omui.agent, mlibs.agent, omui.semantic and openkal's rights table 16% of the code, its JSON and the screenshot's PNG encoder; its code by owner otherwise as terminal's — omui.view 20%, the view's pixel parts 22%, the standard library's instantiations 15%. What brings it down: the first tier's levers, and the endpoint's own share (size design §5.4); tests/bench/competitors/terminal/README.md

links_why: The packages built into the program (B5): a change to this list is a change to what the smallest terminal application with an agent endpoint carries, said in review. Owed: what only pixels use — mrender.raster, mrender.vector, mrender.graph, mrender.text, hanim.visual, mlibs.image and its decoders (mcpplibs.mwrap.libjpeg_turbo, .libpng, .libwebp; compat.libpng, compat.libwebp, compat.zlib), mlibs.pipeline, mlibs.rhi and the solver (mlibs.dynamics, mlibs.simulation) — reached through omui.view and hanim (terminal design §9 step ③, B6)
